Section 1: The Premise of the Company

JD.com, Inc. operates China's leading supply chain-based technology and e-commerce platform. Unlike peer platforms operating purely asset-light marketplace models, JD.com constructed a self-operated direct-sales (1P) retail engine backed by a nationwide, proprietary fulfillment and logistics network (JD Logistics). This integrated infrastructure allows JD to control product sourcing, quality assurance, pricing, warehousing, and last-mile delivery, establishing an consumer value proposition centered on speed, authenticity, and customer service.

The operational engine is anchored by four primary operational metrics monitored by management and equity owners:

  • Annual Active Customers (AAC): Surpassed 700 million active users in late 2025 / early 2026, delivering steady double-digit user momentum and shopping frequency gains across China's Tier 1 through Tier 6 cities.
  • JD Retail Gross & Operating Margins: Expanded to record promotional levels of 18.5% gross margin and 4.6% non-GAAP operating margin, representing 17 consecutive quarters of year-over-year gross margin expansion.
  • Product vs. Service Revenue Mix: Net service revenues (marketplace, advertising, and 3P logistics services) grew over 20% year-over-year, driving a structural mix shift toward higher-margin commission and ad take-rates.
  • Fulfillment & Logistics Scale: Operates over 1,600 warehouses totaling ~32 million square meters of fulfillment space, leveraging automated AI sorting and over 300,000 internal logistics staff to maintain low unit fulfillment costs.

Economic Moat & Pricing Power: JD's durable competitive advantage rests on tollbridge scale economics and massive supply chain switching costs. By directly managing supply chain procurement for 3C electronics, home appliances, and supermarket FMCG items, JD commands immense volume purchasing leverage over manufacturers. Concurrently, its proprietary last-mile logistics network creates a structural moat that cannot be replicated without decades of heavy capital commitment, ensuring superior delivery speed and service consistency during peak shopping festivals.

Executive Leadership Commentary & 4-Quarter Trajectory

Sandy Xu, Chief Executive Officer: "Q2 marked a definitive turning point for our profitability trajectory. Our non-GAAP net income attributable to ordinary shareholders surged by 21% year-on-year to RMB 8.9 billion, driven by both JD Retail's healthy margin expansion and JD Food Delivery's loss reduction of over 50% through improved subsidy efficiency and unit economics. Our commitment to high-quality development and supply chain efficiency positions us to re-accelerate top-line momentum across core retail categories."

Ian Su Shan, Chief Financial Officer: "We are entering a much healthier free cash flow cycle, with trailing twelve-month free cash flow reaching RMB 31.8 billion, supported by disciplined working capital management and normalized trade-in cash outflows. We remain fully committed to disciplined capital return, having repurchased $1.0 billion in shares during the first half of the year while executing our annual cash dividend."

Current State of Play & Cash Generation Reality: JD.com is at an operational inflection point. After navigating macroeconomic digestion in 3C electronics and home appliances, the business has successfully re-aligned its cost structure. Gross margins reached near all-time highs of 17.1% at the consolidated group level, while new ventures (such as local on-demand food delivery and international Joybuy initiatives) reduced operating losses by over 50% year-over-year through improved subsidy discipline.

From an audited cash flow perspective, trailing twelve-month GAAP Operating Cash Flow reached ¥59.0 billion RMB ($8.25 billion USD at 7.15 RMB/USD). Deducting ¥12.7 billion RMB ($1.78 billion USD) in total LTM capital expenditures and treating ¥5.0 billion RMB ($0.70 billion USD) of Stock-Based Compensation as an uncompromised cash cost yields an audited Baseline Owner Earnings (OE₁) of $5.77 billion USD (¥41.3 billion RMB).

Fortress Balance Sheet: As of the latest reported period (Q2 2026, ended June 30, 2026), JD holds ¥235.1 billion RMB ($32.88 billion USD) in cash, restricted cash, and short-term investments. Against ¥62.5 billion RMB ($8.74 billion USD) in total funded debt, lease commitments, and minor M&A obligations, JD maintains an unencumbered net cash balance of $24.14 billion USD (¥172.6 billion RMB). Distributed across approximately 1,390 million American Depositary Shares (ADSs) outstanding (where 1 ADS = 2 Class A ordinary shares), this provides a net balance sheet cash backing of $17.37 per ADS, offering a substantial margin of safety for permanent capital investors.

Section 2: 3 Probable Business Stories

Based on the company's core premise, reported operational metrics, financial filings, and 4-quarter earnings trajectory, here are 3 distinct, probable fundamental paths that cover 90%–95% of probable business outcomes over the next 3–5 years:

📖 Story 1: Core Supply Chain Efficiency & Monetization Shift (Base Case)

In this steady-state baseline trajectory, JD.com leverages its unassailable supply chain infrastructure and authentic 1P product positioning while successfully executing its operational pivot toward third-party (3P) marketplace services and cost discipline. High-margin net service revenues (marketplace commission, advertising, and 3P logistics) outpace 1P product sales, expanding group gross margins. Concurrently, new ventures—such as local on-demand food delivery and international Joybuy initiatives—continue their steady trajectory of loss reduction through rational subsidy management, allowing core retail profitability to flow directly to cash flow.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: Annual Active Customers (AAC) expand steadily from ~700 million to ~800 million over 5 years (a ~2.7% CAGR), supported by moderate user penetration in Tier 3–6 cities and double-digit shopping frequency gains among 36+ million JD PLUS members. Driven by 3P marketplace service revenue growing at ~8%–10% annually and 1P general merchandise posting mid-single-digit gains, consolidated net revenue grows from the baseline of $181.66B USD (¥1,298.9B RMB) to approximately $222.00B USD by Year 5 (a ~4.1% revenue CAGR).

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Group gross margin expands from 17.1% to 18.5% as 3P marketplace take-rates and advertising yields rise. COGS efficiency improves through automated warehouse sorting and reduced fulfillment expense per unit. Non-GAAP operating margin improves from 1.6% to 3.2%. Maintenance and automation CapEx stabilizes at ~$1.90B USD annually, while Stock-Based Compensation is disciplined at ~$0.75B USD. Operating cash flow expands to $12.00B USD, generating Year 5 Owner Earnings of $9.35B USD ($12.00B OCF - $1.90B CapEx - $0.75B SBC), representing an 10.1% annual cash generation growth rate.

Key Milestones to Watch: Continued year-over-year gross margin expansion in JD Retail (target >19.0%); sustained double-digit growth in marketplace and marketing service revenues; and narrowing operating losses in New Businesses toward breakeven.

📖 Story 2: Platform Ecosystem Expansion & High-Margin Monetization (Bull Case)

In this operational super-cycle trajectory, JD.com successfully transforms from a direct-sales retailer into China's premier hybrid supply chain platform. Merchants rapidly adopt JD's merchant ecosystem due to lower platform fees and superior fulfillment logistics, driving 3P GMV to exceed 1P GMV. AI-driven targeted advertising dramatically increases ad take-rates across general merchandise and supermarket categories. Furthermore, local on-demand delivery (JD Food Delivery) achieves structural unit profitability, while international logistics assets (Joybuy) attain meaningful global scale, turning legacy drag into an operational profit tailwind.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: AAC scales past 860 million active users with surging order frequency. Higher-margin 3P marketplace and logistics service revenues compound at a ~13%–15% CAGR. Combined with a cyclical recovery in high-ticket 3C electronics and home appliance trade-in replacement cycles, consolidated net revenue scales from $181.66B USD to $252.00B USD by Year 5 (a ~6.8% revenue CAGR).

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Structural revenue mix shift toward 3P services lifts group gross margins to 20.2%. High operational leverage across the 1,600+ warehouse network expands consolidated operating margin to 4.8% (with JD Retail operating margins reaching 6.2%). Growth CapEx increases modestly to ~$2.20B USD per year for automated regional distribution centers, while SBC is capped at ~$0.80B USD. GAAP operating cash flow accelerates to $16.50B USD, yielding Year 5 Owner Earnings of $13.50B USD ($16.50B OCF - $2.20B CapEx - $0.80B SBC).

Key Milestones to Watch: 3P marketplace GMV growth outpacing 1P GMV for 8 consecutive quarters; advertising revenue expanding at >15% YoY; and positive operating income from New Businesses and international fulfillment operations.

📖 Story 3: Intense Retail Price Competition & Macro Drag (Bear Case)

In this challenging operational trajectory, persistent macroeconomic softness in China and aggressive price wars from live-commerce and discount platforms (e.g., PDD, Douyin) force JD to maintain heavy user subsidies and promotional discounts to protect retail market share. Consumer trading-down behavior suppresses Average Order Value (AOV) in high-margin general merchandise. Furthermore, sluggish housing and consumer durables turnover dampens demand for premium 3C electronics and home appliances, stalling gross margin progression and requiring ongoing defensive capital outlays.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: Active customer acquisition slows, with AAC plateauing around 730 million users. Price discounting compresses AOV, offsetting modest shopping frequency gains. Top-line consolidated net revenue expands at a sluggish ~1.2% CAGR over 5 years, creeping from $181.66B USD to $193.00B USD by Year 5.

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Defensive platform subsidies and lower 1P gross spreads compress group gross margin back to 15.8%. Operating margins remain constrained at 1.1% as marketing expenses scale up to defend user traffic. Maintenance CapEx to operate and renew nationwide fulfillment infrastructure remains mandatory at ~$1.85B USD annually, with SBC at ~$0.70B USD. GAAP operating cash flow contracts to $7.20B USD, resulting in Year 5 Owner Earnings compressing to $4.65B USD ($7.20B OCF - $1.85B CapEx - $0.70B SBC).

Key Milestones to Watch: Compression of JD Retail gross margins below 17.0%; stagnation in annual active user growth; and re-escalation of quarterly operating losses in local on-demand retail ventures.

Step-by-Step Mathematical Proofs Across the 3 Paths

Story 1 ($96.58): JD leverages its direct 1P logistics engine while executing a high-margin pivot toward 3P marketplace commissions and ad monetization. New ventures narrow operating losses through disciplined subsidy management, expanding group operating margins and lifting Year 5 Owner Earnings to $9.35B USD. Starting from normalized baseline Owner Earnings of $5,770.0M compounding at +10.1% annually over 5 years (reaching $9,347.7M in Year 5), the discounted cash flows total $29,351.8M at a 9.5% discount rate. Capitalizing Year 5 terminal cash flow at 2.00% terminal growth produces a terminal value of $127,128.4M (PV $80,755.5M). Operating enterprise value equals $110,107.3M, or $79.21 per ADS across 1,390.0M diluted ADSs. Adding unencumbered net balance sheet cash of +$17.37 per ADS yields an exact intrinsic fair value of $79.21 + $17.37 = $96.58 per ADS.

Story 2 ($130.87): Rapid merchant adoption drives higher-margin 3P marketplace GMV to outpace direct 1P sales, expanding consolidated gross and operating margins. Local on-demand delivery achieves unit profitability while European retail integration (Ceconomy) accelerates global logistics scale, driving Year 5 Owner Earnings to $13.50B USD. Starting from an optimized baseline of $5,770.0M compounding at +18.5% annually (reaching $13,499.5M in Year 5), the discounted cash flows total $36,822.4M at 9.5% discount rate. Capitalizing terminal cash flow at 2.25% yields a terminal value of $190,389.4M (PV $120,940.6M). Total operating enterprise value is $157,763.0M ($113.50 per ADS). Adding net cash of +$17.37 per ADS yields $113.50 + $17.37 = $130.87 per ADS.

Story 3 ($54.05): Persistent macroeconomic softness in China and aggressive price discounting from live-commerce competitors suppress Average Order Value and 1P gross spreads. Ongoing promotional subsidies and mandatory fulfillment maintenance CapEx compress operating cash flow, dragging Year 5 Owner Earnings down to $4.65B USD. Modeling a depressed baseline of $5,770.0M contracting at -4.2% annually (declining to $4,648.6M in Year 5), discounted cash flows total $19,168.9M at a 10.5% hurdle rate. Capitalizing terminal cash flow at 1.50% yields a terminal value of $52,426.0M (PV $31,822.6M). Total operating enterprise value drops to $50,991.5M ($36.68 per ADS). Adding unencumbered net cash of +$17.37 per ADS provides a protective valuation floor of $36.68 + $17.37 = $54.05 per ADS.
